tickets.title: Cursor support through an owned interactive ACP gateway
tickets.body:
Deliver Cursor parity with Agent Director through the shipped `agent-director cursor-host` gateway running as the Cursor row’s own interactive tmux pane process, extending the final amended b.ssz contract across existing caller surfaces without a default agent or screen classification. Scope includes strict ownership and coupled lifetime, ordered pane input, durable permission relay and automatic question denial, latest-only resume/current-life history, installation/runtime validation, help/child callers and provisional group isolation; R1/R2/R4/R6 remain build/acceptance obligations and R5 account/key/platform checks remain NOT CHECKED LIVE until operator-authorized acceptance, with no group-profile or untested-platform release claim. Requirements are defined PRD t1.ftd.y5 and SRD t1.ftd.hj plus the FINAL 2026-10-13 evidence disposition: R3 is closed by Gabe’s question-tool-off/enforced-by-denial decision, and this plan creates draft Epics only, with no hatch, tasks or build.

## do-bee progress

**Epics done**:
- t1.jf1.3e E1 owned launch: source f4f41fd3; status `done`; accepted Docker, applicable formal and both live cases.
- t1.jf1.c1 E2: all Tasks xi/cz/3p `done`; final source b8236bbc1b4a881c3a810d31a865dc8c9530c1d6; Integration Suites: passed, Docker16/16, cursor-relay10/10; TLA+ not applicable. Epic status deliberately `active`: user owns closure.
**Next**: t1.jf1.r8 — user explicitly authorizes scoped E3 hatch/build now, despite E2's user-owned active status and later draft siblings.
**Open decisions/questions**: None blocking E3. No new E2 authenticated receipt is inferred from Docker acceptance.
**Notes for the next session**: Current feature/b.ftd checkout is authorized; local commits only, never push. Sandbox units here; Docker groups and changed-model-only TLA via user scheduler. Real AD stores and Cursor credentials untouched. Preserve b8236bbc bounded answer acquisition and confirmed waiting admission. Later Epics untouched.

## Superseding gate policy — Gabe, 2026-10-15
TLA+ is a design check, not a code test. Include TLA+ jobs in this Task gate ONLY if the Task changes TLA+ model files under spec/tla/**; run only affected models/suites and explain why in SCHEDULER-HANDOFF.md. If none changed, state TLA+ not applicable and schedule no TLA+ jobs. Docker gate remains required. Model assessment still maps realcontroller transitions; do not invent modelchanges merely to force a formal run. This user directive supersedes earlier blanket full-tier/Codex baseline handoff text.

tickets.title: E3 — Take over the pane with ordered prompts and safe conversation controls
tickets.body:
## Outcome and scope
A human and AD caller share one editable pane input controller: successive multiline prompts run in order and interruption or conversation rotation never misroutes queued work.
Maps PRD AC-3/4/5/10/15; SR-0.2, SR-3, SR-4, SR-6.2; R1/R4 interaction acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria / demo
1. In real tmux attach/type, bracketed paste and two successive multiline send-keys submissions preserve Unicode/newlines as separate complete prompts, without lost, duplicated, glued or carried text. Attach/detach and CLI/MCP caller restart retain the conversation; inspect the same output through read-pane.
2. While one ACP turn runs, mix human and automated follow-ups. One observable order and FIFO execution after the turn and outstanding decisions finish is shown in the transcript/protocol trace. Ordinary follow-up never cancels an active turn, and every queued submission is bound to launch and confirmed conversation at acceptance.
3. Give control commands/interruption priority while preserving observable input order. Interrupt cancels the active turn, its decisions and every not-started prompt, visibly identifying each cancellation; it preserves identity and cannot automatically restart work. Repeat with permission and plan dialogs and verify existing pending/hash/dialog/pause guards.
4. Typed /clear and /new cancel work/queue, request a fresh session and change row identity/history only after authoritative confirmation. During rotation hold new input from submission; a failed rotation visibly refuses it and sends it to neither old nor new session. Old completion/session/child events do not replace the confirmed main identity or end a continuing launch.
5. /exit is a terminal command, not model text; /exit and pause visibly cancel the queue and report ended only after real termination. Kill/crash cannot auto-replay transient queue entries. Persist ordered protected transcript records of submissions, cancellations, updates and outcomes and preserve previous conversation history within the same life; persistence failure is visible.
6. Demonstrate question attempts remain automatic denials, with no question-answer UI, while actual permission/plan choices retain their request identity and fallback behavior from E2. A dialog appearing between capture and key delivery retains the inherited, documented safeguard limit rather than an invented guarantee.
7. Acceptance artifact includes actual terminal actions plus correlated session/prompt ids and exact sent text. Emitted JSON alone cannot satisfy attach/paste/control acceptance; synthetic protocol edge cases are separately labelled.

## Implementation/test and doc owners
Extend cursorfix terminal sequence builders and real-tmux newRealTmux/newClientWith/startSession helpers; add table-driven queue/control/failure races and stale-session conditional-write cases beside runtime tests. Own integration slug cursor-pane-controls. docs/usage.md owns input/takeover/commands; docs/permissions.md owns input guards; docs/caller-contract.md/operator-actions.md own failed controls and recovery; architecture owns controller ordering and atomic session rotation.
## Definition of done and execution boundary
This is a draft capability Epic, not authorization to build now. Future implementation must leave the codebase working and all existing tests passing; preserve Claude/Codex behavior and the final t1.ssz.qi amendments. Use existing composition/classifier/store/API seams, machine-readable errors, conditional launch/life writes, parameterized SQL, protected paths and no secret or raw-label leakage. All public CLI/MCP/Go/TypeScript parameters remain in parity through pkg/api; no default agent, screen classification, unrelated-controller gate bypass or new public control API.
Apply docs/engineering-guide.md and docs/test-writing-guide.md within this Epic: behavioral tests for new behavior/functions and error paths, table-driven shared factories, no helper/meta-tests or copied suites; extend SR-10 helpers, isolate HOME/store/socket/processes with unique ids, and add sandboxguard to state/exec packages. pkg/api tests declare parallel or a serial reason; Bun remains sequential. New/changed recovery advice gets a literal-follow test. If persistence changes, follow docs/migration-guide.md: guarded one-transaction-per-hop migration plus current fresh DDL, authorized upgrade twice/reentry, rollback/refusal/data-preservation and fresh/migrated convergence tests.
Create this capability's shell-executable integration collector/cases in tickets/testplans using the existing guide convention and register its slug in test/docker-epics.txt; each case maps AC/SR and emits deterministic JSON evidence, uses isolated fixtures and /opt/driver/sql.sh. Future execution is through operator-scheduled sandbox/Docker jobs (and any applicable existing model checks), never host tests/binaries or local Docker/TLC. Completion evidence includes all existing tests green plus affected CLI/MCP/Bun/real-tmux cases, supported runtime/platform and timing where relevant; label captured versus synthetic evidence. No test or acceptance touches personal credentials.
Update only the named existing doc owners below, current behavior once per owner, with links instead of duplication; no new user manual, no guide-file feature edits except SR-11.1's narrowly required CLI-only exception inventory/rationale maintenance, no .claude edits, and generated references only via existing descriptions/generation. Update docs/architecture.md for changed boundaries and require reuse of any new reusable component. Future commits use the Plan Bee id b.jf1 as conventional-commit scope. No release/parity claim from unrun or synthetic-only acceptance.

tickets.title: PRD
tickets.body:
# Cursor support in agent-director

## Problem Statement

Users with a Cursor budget cannot manage Cursor agents through agent-director (AD) with the state tracking, permission relay, lifecycle controls and groups available to Claude Code and Codex users. They need the same AD workflow for Cursor.

## Goals

- Add Cursor with feature parity with AD's Claude Code and Codex support, including state tracking, permission relay, kill, pause, resume and groups.
- Run Cursor inside the agent tmux pane, the common substrate for AD agents, whichever route the SRD chooses.
- Keep the product as simple as parity permits, extending existing AD controls and caller contracts.

## Non-Goals / Out of Scope

- A replacement transcript display.
- Repeating b.ssz's generic naming migration or implementing Codex again.
- New billing controls, model purchasing or account administration.
- Features beyond existing AD parity unless stated here.

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**Existing AD contract and agent selection.**

- This work builds on b.ssz and PRD t1.ssz.qi, including its final approved amendments of 2026-10-12. Their generic agent selection, naming, launch-path, template, environment, pre-trust, ownership and lifecycle rules apply to Cursor. Those final amendments take precedence over older dependency text.
- Callers can explicitly select `cursor` wherever an agent is selected, including templates. Cursor appears as the row's agent on the existing CLI, MCP, library, client and operator surfaces. There is no default agent.
- Cursor uses the same argument and template precedence rules as the existing agents. Arguments must not silently override AD's required behavior or change the SRD-selected launch route into another operating mode.
- Users can install and use AD on a host with Cursor as its only supported agent. Cursor has the same optional launch-path control and missing-program behavior as the existing agents.

**Interaction and state.**

- Cursor runs inside its agent tmux pane; users can inspect the pane with `read-pane`.
- Users must be able to attach to the agent tmux pane and take over by typing into Cursor normally, whichever route the SRD chooses.
- `send-keys` submits a multiline message intact as one prompt. Repeated sends do not duplicate earlier text or join it to the next message. Existing safeguards for pending agents and possible dialogs still apply.
- Cursor rows use AD's existing states with their existing meanings. Callers can distinguish work in progress, readiness for input, a permission decision, an ended agent and a missing agent. Question behavior follows the contract below.
- A fresh Cursor session reports in when its session starts. A login screen stays `pending`; a running agent that has not reported stays `pending`, noted `unreported`. Resume does not require an immediate startup report and may stay pending until the next prompt.
- A completed or interrupted turn returns the row to the appropriate existing state. Only the row's own agent may change its state; unrelated agents and their activity must not change it.
- Session identity, transcript access and history follow the active conversation. Cursor's `/clear` and `/new` preserve prior-session history within the current life and move the row to the new conversation when reported. Activity by a subagent does not replace the main conversation.

**Permissions and questions.**

- Cursor supports AD's permission relay, including `check_permission`, inspecting a request, allowing or denying it, delivery status, fallback to the pane and recording a pane answer. This covers every kind of permission request in the supported Cursor experience, including requests arising from subagents.
- Callers receive the requested action and available inputs without fabricated details. Decisions apply only to the intended open request and follow AD's existing duplicate-decision and delivery guarantees.
- Permission handling retains AD's existing fail-closed guarantees, timeout behavior and protection against sending ordinary prompts or pausing through unresolved dialogs. A failure or uncertain delivery must not be reported as a successful approval.
- Caller and template permission lists are either honored or clearly refused with actionable guidance to Cursor's own permission rules. No entry is silently ignored; unsupported lists are refused both when creating a template and when launching from a call or template.
- Gabe’s superseding decision, 2026-10-13, R3 option (a): accept question tool off in practice. The cursor-host gateway never advertises question support; any question that reaches AD, including one that falls back to a permission request, is denied automatically; docs describe Cursor as question tool off, enforced by denial, rather than never offered. This applies with `disable_ask_user` on or off, fresh or resumed, and under enabling policies. Questions are never offered for caller/pane approval. This accepted Cursor-specific amendment replaces the earlier pre-execution prevention/native-availability promise; Claude/Codex behavior is unchanged.

**Lifecycle and history.**

- `pause` ends Cursor's current session under the existing pause contract. `kill` retains AD's strict ownership checks and exact success guarantees: it affects only the intended launch and does not claim success when the existing contract requires failure.
- Existing documented limits of kill remain explicit, including work started by an agent that can survive a successful kill. A surviving hook must not be mistaken for a living main agent or be allowed to change a later launch's state.
- `resume` continues only the last agent's latest reported conversation with its saved configuration. A missing latest conversation is reported without falling back to an older one.
- Same-agent reuse preserves session history and subagent records within the current life. Switching to or from Cursor starts a new life and permanently gives up AD resume of earlier sessions; switching back never restores them. A switching launch that asks to resume starts fresh without error, with dropped arguments reported under the inherited contract.
- Session history and subagent records show only the current life. AD-agent children remain associated with their parent across a switch. Failed reuse, permission-request cleanup and the trail retain the dependency's final amended behavior.
- Cursor supports the existing lifecycle, status, cleanup, labels, help, trail and administration operations on all corresponding AD surfaces. The subagent view either shows accurate supported Cursor subagent information or explicitly reports tracking unsupported with no subagents, under the existing contract. It must not invent activity, states or an unknown state. Subagent permission relay remains required independently of tracking support. Codex remains untracked with no subagents shown.
- With help enabled, Cursor receives the existing AD guidance at session start and after session changes. Guidance is restored after compaction, or documentation records the difference as permitted by the inherited contract. A Cursor caller can use AD's CLI and MCP workflows with correct parent-child association and the same tmux-server behavior as other AD callers.

**Groups and accounts.**

- Many Cursor agents can run concurrently using one group's login and rules. Another group can use a different login and rules without acquiring the first group's credentials or group-specific settings.
- Authentication renewal for one agent must not invalidate another agent's login or overwrite the user's personal login. AD lifecycle operations do not sign users out or alter personal account configuration.
- Group setup and reuse fit the existing environment and template workflow. Resume retains the original group's configuration and conversation.
- Users receive a clear explanation of which personal, project or organization policies also apply and their precedence. Group configuration must not be described as a stronger isolation boundary than the product provides.
- Users can run the models available to their Cursor account against their Cursor budget. Documentation explains the account and billing context, including when a separately configured provider bills elsewhere, without adding AD billing controls.

### Edge Cases and Error Handling

- Missing programs, login requirements, invalid configuration, invalid arguments and failed launches produce the existing corresponding AD outcomes and actionable errors; nothing silently substitutes another agent or account.
- A stale session identity on exit after `/clear` or `/new` must not leave an exited agent classified as live, or a continuing agent classified as ended. Session changes and resume retain the ownership guarantees.
- Interrupted turns, human answers at the pane, relay delivery failures and timeouts preserve the existing caller safeguards and expose the outcome accurately.
- Authentication expiry or group configuration problems must not silently fall back to another group's or the user's personal credentials.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- Liveness is determined from processes, and no screen text is classified to infer states, dialogs or prompts.
- Cursor support preserves AD's existing ownership, security, privacy and secret-handling guarantees. Existing Claude Code and Codex behavior remains compatible with the final approved dependency contract.
- Spawn, resume and other operations remain within existing client time limits on AD-supported hosts where Cursor runs.

### UI/UX Requirements

- Existing help and documentation explain selecting Cursor, installation, launch configuration, groups, permissions, recovery and the latest-session resume rule alongside the corresponding existing-agent guidance.
- Status and errors use AD's existing vocabulary and distinguish pending startup from readiness. Cursor runs inside the agent tmux pane regardless of the selected route.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cursor can be selected directly or through a template on all existing caller surfaces; precedence, validation and no-default behavior match the inherited contract, and rows identify Cursor correctly.
- [ ] A Cursor-only installation works, the launch-path setting is honored, and missing or invalid launches produce the expected AD outcomes.
- [ ] Cursor runs inside the agent tmux pane; `read-pane` and successive multiline `send-keys` work without lost, duplicated or glued text.
- [ ] Users can attach to the agent tmux pane and take over by typing into Cursor normally, whichever route the SRD chooses, with documentation explaining human takeover.
- [ ] Fresh launch reports at session startup; login and unreported startup remain pending; resumed sessions can remain pending until prompted; working, waiting, permission and terminal states retain their documented meanings.
- [ ] Every supported Cursor permission kind can be inspected and answered through AD. Allow, deny, timeout, duplicate decision, uncertain delivery, pane fallback and recorded human answers preserve existing relay and prompt-safety guarantees.
- [ ] Caller and template permission-list entries are honored or refused with actionable guidance to Cursor's own rules; unsupported entries are refused at template creation and at launch, including from a saved template, and none are silently ignored.
- [ ] The Cursor gateway never advertises question support and automatically denies every question reaching AD, including permission fallback, for both suppression setting values, fresh/resumed sessions and enabling policies. Caller or pane approvals cannot answer a question. Documentation says question tool off, enforced by denial, and does not claim never offered (Gabe’s 2026-10-13 R3 option (a)).
- [ ] Pause ends the intended session; kill meets its existing ownership and success contract, including errors and documented survivor limits; unrelated launches are untouched and surviving hooks cannot change a later launch's state.
- [ ] `/clear` and `/new` rotate conversation identity and history correctly; stale exit identities never leave a dead agent live or a continuing agent ended.
- [ ] Resume restores the latest conversation and group configuration only; a missing latest conversation is reported without fallback. Same-agent reuse retains history, switches clear the current life's history, and switching back with a resume request starts fresh without reviving earlier sessions. AD-agent children remain listed across switches.
- [ ] Concurrent agents in one group share its login and rules while another group uses its own; renewal and lifecycle operations preserve other agents' and the user's personal login, and failures never silently use another account.
- [ ] The Cursor subagent view shows accurate supported information or explicitly reports tracking unsupported with no subagents; it invents no activity or states, including an unknown state. Subagent permissions are relayed regardless of tracking support, and Codex remains untracked with no subagents shown.
- [ ] Existing lifecycle and administration surfaces, labels, trail and Cursor-originated CLI/MCP child launches satisfy the existing AD contracts. With help enabled, guidance appears at session start and after session changes; after compaction it is restored or the difference is documented.
- [ ] Documentation covers the Cursor workflow, recovery, group-policy precedence and billing context; no group isolation or operation outcome is overstated. Claude and Codex contracts remain intact, and operations meet existing time limits without screen-based state classification.

## Assumptions

- b.ssz and the final approved amendments to t1.ssz.qi provide the baseline; this PRD adds Cursor to that product contract.
- Risk for the SRD: the SRD chooses the terminal or ACP route after a research round, and must meet the parity requirements.

tickets.title: Admit and execute bounded, conversation-bound prompt submissions in order
tickets.body:
## Context

The terminal preserves Unicode, literal newlines and bracketed paste, but promptAdmission reserves only one idle prompt and session.go refuses busy follow-ups. E2 established independently verified committed-waiting admission and saved initial-prompt priority. Extend that shared path while preserving startup, permission and ownership safeguards.

Plan b.jf1; Idea b.ftd; approved PRD t1.ftd.y5; SRD t1.ftd.hj; Epic t1.jf1.r8. Planning artifacts and PM approval are in tickets/handoff/b.ftd/Plans/b.jf1/e3/planning/. No E4 resume/load/reuse/life-switch, installation, groups or help work. SendKeys literal text and Enter remain separate operations; no arbitrary concurrent-caller atomicity promise.

## Execution boundary

User: “make test-sandbox is yours, Docker groups and any TLA+ come to me via a scheduler handoff, TLA+ only if spec/tla changes.”

Execute repository tests, scripts and binaries only through `make sandbox` or `make test-sandbox`, with fresh isolated HOME, AD store, socket and owned processes. Never touch the real `~/.config/agent-director` or `~/.agent-director`. Never access/edit `.claude`, log in/out, or read, copy, hash or change credentials. Existing Cursor login stays as is; separately authorized live work runs isolated under `~/ad-codex/ftd/` and stops if login is unreachable. No host tests/binaries, local Docker TESTPLAN groups/collectors, TLC, parsers, scheduler submissions or pushes. Only actual changed `spec/tla/**` model inputs warrant affected-model scheduler jobs, with reasons; do not manufacture model changes or baseline jobs. AD never derives state, identity, permissions or liveness from screen text. Local commits are coordinator-owned on feature/b.ftd with scope b.jf1. Technical decisions are recorded in the SRD; escalate only genuine product questions.


## What Needs to Change

- Represent complete submissions in one observable acceptance order with bounded resource use and explicit refusal when capacity or eligibility prevents admission.
- Bind accepted submissions to current launch and confirmed conversation at acceptance; preserve complete text and submission identity independent from later ACP request IDs.
- Run ordinary submissions FIFO, one active prompt, after prior turn and outstanding decision constraints permit progression.
- Reuse reporter.verifyReport, runtime/pane verification and durable request predicates; preserve committed-waiting handoff and saved initial-prompt priority.
- Separate ordinary submissions from permission/plan choices and controls. Keep /clear and /new visibly refused in Task1.
- Preserve public send-keys/read-pane/pause contracts; no new public Cursor control API.

## Key Files

- internal/cursorhost/admission.go
- internal/cursorhost/terminal_linux.go
- internal/cursorhost/terminal_other.go
- internal/cursorhost/session.go
- internal/cursorhost/report.go
- internal/cursorhost/requests.go
- internal/cursorhost/protocol.go
- pkg/api/sendkeys.go — contract dependency
- internal/tmux/calls_socket.go — contract dependency
- internal/store/request_proof.go — durable eligibility dependency

## Acceptance Criteria

- Human typing, bracketed paste and successive multiline API submissions preserve Unicode/newlines as distinct complete prompts without duplication or carried text.
- Follow-ups accepted during a running turn execute FIFO without cancelling that turn.
- No submission starts against an unconfirmed, changed, retired or mismatched launch/conversation; input consumed before startup eligibility cannot become future work after startup.
- Committed-waiting reservation survives the hook tail; saved initial prompt retains priority.
- Still-open permission/plan decisions block dispatch. Turn completion, acknowledgement, native claim or pipe output cannot manufacture proof that unknown-origin requests are gone.
- Saturation explicitly refuses without silently dropping/replacing accepted work or indefinitely blocking work/controls.
- Pending, pane-hash, permission-answer and dialog safeguards remain effective.

tickets.title: Prioritize interruption and shutdown with finite, explicit queue cancellation
tickets.body:
## Context

Current interruption/local exit/eligible pause retain a fixed three-second cancellation deadline. Queuing creates races between input consumption, turn completion, pending output and cancellation; bounded shared input channel and synchronous reports require attention. In-memory request retirement is not durable proof a dialog disappeared.

Plan b.jf1; Idea b.ftd; approved PRD t1.ftd.y5; SRD t1.ftd.hj; Epic t1.jf1.r8. Planning artifacts and PM approval are in tickets/handoff/b.ftd/Plans/b.jf1/e3/planning/. E2 all Tasks are done and its accepted source is b8236bbc; E2 Epic remains active because the user owns its closure. User explicitly authorized scoped E3 hatch/build despite that status and later draft siblings. Preserve E2 bounded answer guards, committed-waiting admission, unknown-origin proof holds, acknowledgement-before-output, finite cancellation and public input safeguards. No E4 resume/load/reuse/life-switch, installation, groups or help work. SendKeys literal text and Enter remain separate operations; no arbitrary concurrent-caller atomicity promise.

## Execution boundary

User: “make test-sandbox is yours, Docker groups and any TLA+ come to me via a scheduler handoff, TLA+ only if spec/tla changes.”

Execute repository tests, scripts and binaries only through `make sandbox` or `make test-sandbox`, with fresh isolated HOME, AD store, socket and owned processes. Never touch the real `~/.config/agent-director` or `~/.agent-director`. Never access/edit `.claude`, log in/out, or read, copy, hash or change credentials. Existing Cursor login stays as is; separately authorized live work runs isolated under `~/ad-codex/ftd/` and stops if login is unreachable. No host tests/binaries, local Docker TESTPLAN groups/collectors, TLC, parsers, scheduler submissions or pushes. Only actual changed `spec/tla/**` model inputs warrant affected-model scheduler jobs, with reasons; do not manufacture model changes or baseline jobs. AD never derives state, identity, permissions or liveness from screen text. Local commits are coordinator-owned on feature/b.ftd with scope b.jf1. Technical decisions are recorded in the SRD; escalate only genuine product questions.


## What Needs to Change

- Give interruption and terminal controls priority over waiting ordinary submissions while retaining observable input order.
- Cancel active work, retire outstanding decision-response authority and visibly identify each affected not-started submission cancellation.
- Prevent input consumed during cancellation from automatically restarting work later.
- Preserve the first cancellation deadline through repeated interruption, policy cancellation and authorization-hold release.
- Integrate queue cancellation with local exit, eligible pause, signals, transport/runtime failure and owned shutdown.
- Prevent accepted outbound prompts from starting after cancellation; treat partial/uncertain output honestly, no retry or false zero-delivery assertion.
- Reuse requestController, guarded serialized writer and owned termination/reporting. Unknown-origin durable holds require existing valid proof or owning-spawn end.

## Key Files

- internal/cursorhost/session.go
- internal/cursorhost/admission.go
- internal/cursorhost/terminal_linux.go
- internal/cursorhost/requests.go
- internal/cursorhost/protocol.go
- internal/cursorhost/report.go
- internal/cursorhost/process_linux.go — lifecycle dependency
- pkg/api/pause.go — public guard dependency
- internal/store/cursor_permission.go — authority dependency

## Acceptance Criteria

- Interrupt cancels active and affected not-started work, preserves conversation identity, never automatically restarts work.
- Controls remain effective under ordinary-input/outbound pressure; cancelled queued prompts never later produce prompt calls.
- Repeated interrupts and hold release cannot extend the existing three-second cancellation deadline.
- Cancellation retires queued allow and deny while preserving ack-before-output, both guards, bounded store acquisition/post-wait checks and no uncertain replay.
- Menu choices cannot answer retired requests; independent question denial retains semantics.
- Exit is never model text; exit/eligible pause visibly cancel queue and report ended only after confirmed owned-runtime termination.
- Kill/crash cannot restore transient work; caller restart or attach/detach alone preserves gateway/conversation.
- Public pause/dialog guards and Claude/Codex behavior remain unchanged.

tickets.title: Record the complete submission lifecycle in the protected transcript
tickets.body:
## Context

Existing private JSONL recorder sequences, attributes and synchronizes records, but user_input is written only when a turn starts. Accepted queued work cancelled before start needs durable observable ordering without a replayable queue.

Plan b.jf1; Idea b.ftd; approved PRD t1.ftd.y5; SRD t1.ftd.hj; Epic t1.jf1.r8. Planning artifacts and PM approval are in tickets/handoff/b.ftd/Plans/b.jf1/e3/planning/.
